requirement: Upload a local file with a description field to an HTTP endpoint as multipart form data, refusing files over a size limit before sending and surfacing server errors.
skeleton: Upload limit and timeout constants, an UploadTooLargeError with size and limit, and upload checking the size, opening the file in binary mode and posting data plus a named files tuple, then raising on HTTP errors and returning the JSON.
caption: Uploading a file plus metadata as multipart/form-data with requests. UploadTooLargeError is a ValueError subclass carrying size and limit. upload(session, url, path, *, description, content_type=application/octet-stream) reads the file size with stat and raises UploadTooLargeError when it exceeds MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, 5 MiB, read at call time, before any request is sent. It opens the file in binary mode inside a with block and calls session.post with data holding the description form field, files mapping file to a tuple of the file name, the handle and the content type, and the TIMEOUT constant. raise_for_status turns server errors into requests.HTTPError, and the JSON reply is returned as a dict. The fixture asserts, against a local server parsing the multipart body, that the file part keeps report.csv, text/csv and its non-UTF-8 bytes and the description is a plain field, that the default type is octet-stream, that a file of exactly the limit is sent, that a larger one raises UploadTooLargeError without a request, and that a 500 raises requests.HTTPError.

plan.intent: Attach reports to tickets through a web API
constraints: Files over MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES raise UploadTooLargeError before sending
The file is opened in binary mode and closed after the request
The part carries the file name and content type, default octet-stream
The description is sent as a form field

rationale.teaches: Send multipart uploads with files as a (name, handle, type) tuple plus data fields, open files in binary mode, and validate size before the network call.
rationale.why: Text mode corrupts or fails on binary bytes, putting metadata in the query string loses it from the form, and checking size after upload wastes bandwidth.

ops.docstring: Upload a file with metadata as multipart/form-data using requests.

ops.source:
def upload(
    session: requests.Session,
    url: str,
    path: Path,
    *,
    description: str,
    content_type: str = "application/octet-stream",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """POST ``path`` as the ``file`` part with a ``description`` form field."""
    size = path.stat().st_size
    if size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:
        raise UploadTooLargeError(size, MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES)
    with path.open("rb") as fh:
        resp = session.post(
            url,
            data={"description": description},
            files={"file": (path.name, fh, content_type)},
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    result: dict[str, Any] = resp.json()
    return result

candidates.why_wrong: A file of exactly the size limit is rejected.
Files default to text/plain instead of application/octet-stream.
The description goes into the query string instead of the form body.
A 500 error reply is returned as if the upload succeeded.
The file is opened in text mode and fails on non-UTF-8 bytes.
